title: Automated imaging-based high-throughput screening for small molecules that reverse cellular senescence
protocol: Harvest exponentially growing phoenix-ampho cells by trypsinization with trypsin-EDTA solution.
Plate harvested cells on 60-mm tissue culture dishes at a density of about 10^6 cells/dish.
Dilute 5 µg of plasmid DNA in 700 µl of Opti-MEM I Reduced Serum Medium and mix gently.
Dilute 20 µl of Lipofectamine in 700 µl of Opti-MEM I and mix gently.
Combine diluted DNA solution with diluted Lipofectamine solution and mix by pipetting up and down several times.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove growth medium from phoenix-ampho cells and replace with the DNA-Lipofectamine complex solution.
Rock the plate to distribute the complex evenly.
Incubate cells for 6 h at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with an atmosphere of 5% CO2.
Remove transfection mixture from cells after 6 hours.
Replace with fresh complete medium.
After 18 h, replace the medium with fresh culture medium.
Plate actively proliferating BJ cells, which underwent 30-40 population doublings, in 100-mm culture dishes at 30 h prior to the infection procedure.
Collect virus-containing medium from the transfected packaging cells after 48 h of transfection.
Remove cell debris and aggregated virus by low speed centrifugation for 5 min at 4 °C.
Filter medium through a 0.45-µm cellulose acetate filter.
Dilute the filtered virus-containing medium by mixing it with fresh complete medium in a 4:1 ratio.
Add polybrene to a final concentration of 4 µg/ml and mix gently.
Infect BJ fibroblasts by replacing the culture medium with 10 ml of the diluted virus-containing medium.
Replace the medium with fresh complete medium after 48 h of incubation.
After 48 h, add puromycin at a final concentration of 1 µg/ml for four days for selection.
Replace selection medium with fresh complete medium and incubate cells for three days.
Observe cells under the fluorescence microscope to determine the EGFP signal in the infected cells.
Split cells into 100-mm plates and incubate for seven days until the cells do not divide further and their shapes are changed to flattened enlarged morphology characteristic of cellular senescence.
Ensure that the EGFP signal is still well detected in these cells by using fluorescence microscope.
Subject a small subpopulation of infected BJ cells for SA-β-gal analysis.
Use uninfected BJ cells and BJ cells infected with retrovirus expressing EGFP only as negative controls.
Use BJ cells infected with virus coexpressing TRF2ΔBΔM and EGFP for positive control.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Fix cells with 2% formaldehyde/0.2% glutaraldehyde solution in PBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash cells twice with PBS.
Incubate cells with SA-β-gal staining solution at 37°C without CO₂ supply.
After about 10 h, observe cells under the bright field microscope to determine SA–β–gal staining.
If SA–β–gal staining is weak in BJ cells infected with virus coexpressing TRF2ΔBΔM and EGFP, extend incubation time until staining is marked compared to negative controls.
Wash once with PBS after staining.
Capture cellular images with bright field microscope.
Add compounds from a chemical library to 96-well plates at a final concentration of 1 µg/ml.
Capture live cell images of EGFP-positive BJ cells every 24 hours for six days using an IN Cell Analyzer 1000 autofocusing microscope.
Analyze the captured images using image analysis software to quantify the number and size of cells.

When an increase in cell number and a decrease in cell size, along with the loss of flattened enlarged cellular morphology are detected, validate the senescence reversal effects by subjecting the cells for SA-β-gal staining.
